findings.label: L2B International | SHJ→DEL | 880 searches

findings.label: Priority | LAX→AMD | Ahmedabad
findings.rootCause: The results page fully loaded with 507 flights displayed, but our automation's progress-bar detection timed out before recognising the results, causing a false FAILURE rating.
findings.evidence: All four frames (result screenshot + 3 final video frames) show a fully rendered Etrav results page: 'Showing (507) Flights from Los Angeles (LAX) to Ahmedabad (AMD)', cheapest fare ₹2,18,960.24, fastest fare ₹2,53,529, multiple bookable itineraries (KLM, IndiGo), correct form values (LAX→AMD, 24 Jun–30 Jun, 8 Travellers Economy). There is no loading spinner, no progress bar, no error page, and no blank/empty state — the search completed successfully. The failure was logged solely because our 60-second progress-bar-disappearance check did not detect results before its deadline.
findings.ruleBookEntry: IF results page shows 'Showing (N) Flights' with bookable cards AND no loading bar is visible in final frames → mark as SUCCESS; do NOT raise FAILURE based solely on progress-bar timeout (EQIS_PROGRESSBAR_TIMEOUT_FALSE_NEGATIVE).
findings.eqisFixSuggestion: Add a secondary result-detection check that looks for the 'Showing (N) Flights' heading or at least one 'Book Now' button before concluding a timeout failure; if either selector is present the search should be rated SUCCESS regardless of whether the progress bar CSS class was observed to disappear. Also consider increasing the progress-bar timeout to 90 s for international multi-pax searches, or polling for results every 5 s in parallel with the bar check.

findings.label: L2B International | Makkah | Hotel Search
findings.rootCause: Etrav's hotel autosuggest API returned no dropdown suggestions for 'Mecca'/'Makkah', leaving the destination field in a typed-but-unresolved state with no selectable option, so the search could not proceed.
findings.evidence: All four frames (result screenshot + 3 video frames) show an identical frozen state: the destination field displays the typed text 'Mecca' but no autosuggest dropdown ever appeared beneath it, and the Check-In / Check-Out dates remain empty dashes ('–'). The page never advanced past the hotel search home screen. No dropdown list, no suggestion items, and no error banner are visible — consistent with the autosuggest API silently returning zero results rather than a platform crash.
findings.ruleBookEntry: IF hotel destination field contains typed text AND no autosuggest dropdown rendered AND date fields remain empty AND page does not change across all recorded frames → AUTOSUGGEST_DOWN (etrav-side): Etrav autosuggest API returned no suggestions for the queried destination.

findings.label: L2B Domestic | DEL→SXR | 259,548 searches
findings.rootCause: Etrav's backend returned zero inventory for DEL→SXR on 2026-07-18 with 11 pax (9A+2I), displaying its 'Flight Unavailable' page — the search was correctly formed and submitted.
findings.evidence: All four frames (result screenshot + 3 video frames) are identical: the search form is correctly populated (From: New Delhi (DEL), To: Srinagar (SXR), Departure: 18 Jul'26, Return: 17 Aug'26, 11 Travellers Economy), the URL parameters are well-formed (search_type=SPECIAL_RETURN, adult_count=9, infant_count=2, correct IATA codes), and Etrav rendered its own 'Flight Unavailable' illustration with the message 'We're sorry, but the flight you were looking for is no longer available. This might be due to the flight being fully booked or removed from our system.' Showing (0) Flights is displayed. There is no form input error, no autosuggest failure, no EQIS mis-click — the platform itself returned no inventory.
findings.ruleBookEntry: IF page shows 'Flight Unavailable' illustration AND result count shows '(0) Flights' AND all form fields are correctly filled → ETRAV_ZERO_INVENTORY (etrav-side); do not classify as EQIS failure.

findings.eqisFixSuggestion: Update the result-detection logic to positively check for the 'Showing (\d+) Flights' text or the presence of at least one flight card element as a SUCCESS signal BEFORE concluding a timeout. The 60-second progress-bar-disappearance check should be secondary/fallback, not the sole criterion. findings.label: L2B Domestic | BLR→CCU | 6,590 searches
findings.rootCause: Playwright's page.goto timed out at 45 000 ms waiting for 'domcontentloaded' on https://new.etrav.in/flights, so the automation never reached the form-filling stage; all frames show a fully rendered, blank Etrav flight search page with no fields filled and no Etrav-side error.
findings.evidence: All four frames (3 video + 1 screenshot) are identical: the Etrav flights page loaded correctly (header, nav, hero image, One-Way form with empty 'Where From?', 'Where To?', Departure fields, and a working 'Search Flight' button are all visible). There is no error page, no Oops illustration, no spinner, and no network failure banner. The failure log explicitly states 'page.goto: Timeout 45000ms exceeded' — meaning our Playwright runner hit its own timeout while waiting for domcontentloaded, not because Etrav failed to serve the page.
findings.ruleBookEntry: IF call-log shows 'page.goto: Timeout Nms exceeded' AND frames show a fully rendered Etrav page with no error illustration → EQIS_GOTO_TIMEOUT (eqis-side); the automation's navigation wait timed out, not an Etrav platform failure.
findings.eqisFixSuggestion: 1) Increase the page.goto timeout from 45 000 ms to at least 90 000 ms for the initial navigation, or switch the waitUntil condition from 'domcontentloaded' to 'load' to avoid races with late-firing DOMContentLoaded events. 2) Add a retry-on-timeout wrapper around page.goto so transient slow loads are retried up to 2 times before marking the run as failed. 3) Investigate whether the Playwright browser context is reused across searches and is accumulating memory/open tabs that slow navigation.

findings.label: Priority | ATQ→SHJ | Sharjah
findings.rootCause: The automation typed only 'A' into the 'Where From?' field and then timed out waiting for the elementHandle.type call to complete, leaving the autosuggest stuck on the generic 'Popular Cities' list instead of filtering to ATQ.
findings.evidence: All four frames (video frames + result screenshot) show an identical frozen state: the 'Where From?' field contains only the letter 'A', the autosuggest dropdown is open showing the default Popular Cities list (MAA, AAL, AAR, AAT, AAZ, ABA…) — not an ATQ-specific suggestion — and the 'Where To?' field remains empty with '–'. The field never received the full 'ATQ' string, and Playwright timed out at 30 000 ms on the elementHandle.type('ATQ') call. Etrav's UI is fully rendered and functional; no error page is shown.
findings.ruleBookEntry: IF 'Where From?' field contains only a partial string AND autosuggest shows only generic Popular Cities (not the target IATA code) AND Playwright throws elementHandle.type timeout → EQIS_TYPE_TIMEOUT_ON_ORIGIN_FIELD (eqis-side): automation failed to complete typing into the input element before the 30 s timeout.
findings.eqisFixSuggestion: 1) Before calling elementHandle.type(), ensure the field is properly focused and cleared with elementHandle.click() + elementHandle.fill('') to avoid stale focus issues. 2) Increase the Playwright timeout for this specific type() call to at least 60 000 ms, or switch to page.fill(selector, 'ATQ') which is more reliable. 3) After typing, explicitly wait for the autosuggest list to contain the target IATA code (waitForSelector('[data-iata="ATQ"]', {timeout:15000})) before attempting to click it, to confirm the type operation succeeded.

findings.label: L2B Domestic | BLR→BOM | 8,704 searches
findings.rootCause: The result page loaded successfully with 1146 flights shown, but our automation's result-detection logic failed to recognise the results before its 60-second timeout expired, causing a false-positive failure rating.
findings.evidence: All four frames (the result screenshot and all three final video frames) are identical and clearly show a fully-loaded Etrav results page: 'Showing (1146) Flights from Bangalore (BLR) to Mumbai (BOM)', cheapest fare ₹10,615 | 3h 55m, multiple SpiceJet itineraries rendered, no loading bar visible anywhere on the page. The form fields are correctly populated (BLR→BOM, 22 Jun '26 / 13 Jul '26, 3 Travellers Economy). There is zero evidence of a timeout, spinner, error page, or missing results.
findings.ruleBookEntry: IF result page shows 'Showing (N) Flights' text AND flight cards are rendered AND no loading bar is visible, yet automation reports 'loading bar did not disappear / no result evidence detected' → FALSE_NEGATIVE_RESULT_DETECTION (eqis-side): result-presence selector missed the loaded state.
findings.eqisFixSuggestion: Update the result-detection logic to check for the presence of the 'Showing (N) Flights from … to …' heading (e.g. CSS selector 'h2,div' containing text matching /Showing \(\d+\) Flights/) as a primary success signal, in addition to (or instead of) waiting for the loading progress bar to disappear. Also add a DOM-ready check for at least one flight-card element before declaring a timeout failure.

findings.label: Priority | DEL→RUH | Riyadh
findings.rootCause: Results (299 flights) loaded successfully on Etrav but our automation's result-detection logic failed to recognise the loaded page before the 60-second timeout expired.
findings.evidence: All four frames (result screenshot + 3 video frames) show an identical, fully-rendered Etrav results page: 'Showing (299) Flights from New Delhi (DEL) to Riyadh (RUH)', cheapest fare ₹92,108 | 19h 40m, fastest ₹1,70,555 | 13h 25m, at least two complete flight cards visible with Book Now buttons, correct form fields (DEL→RUH, 23 Jun–6 Jul, 5 Travellers Business Class). There is no loading spinner, no progress bar, no error page, and no blank/empty state in any frame. The platform clearly returned results well within any reasonable timeout window.
findings.ruleBookEntry: IF final frames show a populated Etrav results page (flight count > 0, fare cards visible, no progress bar) AND failure reason cites 'loading progress bar did not disappear' → EQIS_RESULT_DETECTION_MISS (eqis-side): automation timed out waiting for a stale/already-gone progress bar or used a wrong DOM selector to confirm results loaded.
findings.eqisFixSuggestion: Replace the progress-bar-disappearance check as the sole 'results loaded' signal. Instead, use a positive presence check: wait for a selector such as '.showing-flights-count', '.flight-result-card', or the text 'Showing (N) Flights' to appear in the DOM (with a 60 s timeout). If that element is already present when the check begins (bar may have disappeared before the first poll), the detection should succeed immediately. Also add a fallback: if the progress bar is no longer in the DOM at all at the start of polling, treat that as 'already finished' and proceed to result extraction rather than waiting/timing out.

findings.label: L2B Domestic | BOM→CCU | 10,854 searches
findings.rootCause: The result page fully loaded with 104 flights shown, but the EQIS result-detection logic failed to recognize the results and incorrectly reported a loading timeout.
findings.evidence: All four frames (result screenshot + 3 video frames) show a fully rendered Etrav results page: 'Showing (104) Flights from Mumbai (BOM) to Kolkata (CCU)', cheapest fare ₹7,574 | 2h 35m, multiple Book Now buttons visible, filter/sort bar present, and no loading spinner or progress bar anywhere. The page is completely stable across all frames. The failure reason ('Loading progress bar did not disappear within 60 seconds AND no result evidence detected') is contradicted directly by the visual evidence.
findings.ruleBookEntry: IF results page shows 'Showing (N) Flights' header AND Book Now buttons are visible AND no loading bar is present → mark as SUCCESS; the result-detection selector is broken, not Etrav. (EQIS_RESULT_DETECTOR_MISS)
findings.eqisFixSuggestion: Update the result-detection logic to check for the presence of the text 'Showing (' combined with a count > 0 in the results header (e.g., CSS selector: 'text*="Showing"' or XPath containing 'Flights from'), OR check for at least one '.Book Now' button rendered on the page. findings.ruleBookEntry: IF hotel search form destination is filled AND both date fields remain '–' AND no calendar overlay is visible across all frames AND status is AUTOMATION_DATE_INCOMPLETE → HOTEL_DATE_PICKER_OPEN_FAILURE (eqis-side): automation failed to open/interact with the Etrav hotel date picker widget.
findings.eqisFixSuggestion: In pickHotelDateRange: (1) Replace a direct click on the Check-In input with a JS-dispatched mousedown+click combo targeting the calendar icon SVG/button inside the Check-In field container, then wait up to 3000ms for the calendar overlay (e.g. .rdrCalendarWrapper or equivalent) to appear before attempting to select dates. (2) After first attempt fails, re-scroll the field into viewport and retry with a coordinate-based click on the calendar trigger icon. (3) Add an explicit visibility wait for the calendar month grid before proceeding to date cell selection. (4) Log the DOM state of the date field on each failed attempt to capture whether the picker opened but closed prematurely or never opened at all.

findings.label: L2B International | Bangkok | Hotel Search
findings.rootCause: The automation successfully filled the destination ('Bangkok Province') and check-in date ('7 Jul'26') but never populated the Check-Out date field, leaving it as '-', which caused form validation to block the search with 'Check-out date is required'.
findings.evidence: All four frames (3 video + 1 result screenshot) are identical: destination='Bangkok Province', check-in='7 Jul'26', check-out='-' (empty/dash) with a red validation error 'Check-out date is required'. The page never navigated to results. No Etrav error page, no autosuggest failure — the platform correctly rejected an incomplete form. The failure reason 'autosuggest may have failed silently' is a misdiagnosis; the destination was actually filled correctly.
findings.ruleBookEntry: IF hotel form shows destination filled AND check-in filled AND check-out is '-'/empty AND 'Check-out date is required' validation visible → EQIS_CHECKOUT_DATE_NOT_SET (eqis-side): automation failed to write checkout date into the date picker.
findings.eqisFixSuggestion: Ensure the checkout date picker interaction is explicitly awaited and confirmed: after clicking the Check-Out field, wait for the calendar to render, click the correct date cell, verify the field value changes away from '-' before proceeding to click 'Search Hotel'. Add an assertion that checks the Check-Out field text !== '-' and !== '' after the date-selection step; retry the calendar interaction if the assertion fails.

findings.label: L2B Domestic | BOM→BLR | 2,956 searches
findings.rootCause: Our automation failed to select 'Round Trip' and commit the return date; the form remained stuck on 'One Way' with the Return field showing only '–' across all frames, despite 3 internal retries.
findings.evidence: All 4 frames (screenshot + 3 video frames) show an identical state: 'One Way' radio is selected (not 'Round Trip'), the Return? field displays '–' (never populated), departure is correctly set to '30 Jun'26', origin/destination are correctly filled (BOM→BLR), but the trip-type was never switched and the return date calendar was never successfully opened or committed. The Etrav platform itself is fully rendered, responsive, and shows no error — the Search Flight button is visible and enabled. The failure reason logged confirms pickFlightDateRange exhausted all 3 retries.
findings.ruleBookEntry: IF Return? field shows '–' AND trip-type radio still shows 'One Way' AND departure date is filled AND no Etrav error page present → EQIS_RETURN_DATE_NOT_COMMITTED: automation failed to switch to Round Trip and/or interact with the return date calendar (eqis-side).
findings.eqisFixSuggestion: Before calling pickFlightDateRange for return date: (1) explicitly click the 'Round Trip' radio button and wait for the Return? field to become active/enabled (poll until Return? field is no longer disabled or '–' state changes); (2) add a 1000ms stabilisation wait after Round Trip selection before opening the date picker; (3) verify the calendar opens (check for calendar DOM element visibility) before attempting date cell clicks; (4) after date selection, assert Return? field value matches expected date string before marking commit as successful — if assertion fails, re-click the cell rather than retrying from scratch.

findings.label: L2B International | Pattaya | Hotel Search
findings.rootCause: The search completed successfully with 1013 results for Pattaya, but the SearchPulse rating system incorrectly flagged a SUCCESS status as CRITICAL failure with no recorded failure reason.
findings.evidence: All 4 frames (1 result screenshot + 3 video frames) show an identical, fully rendered hotel search results page: destination field shows 'Pattaya', Check-In 9 Jul'26, Check-Out 10 Jul'26, 1 Room / 2 Guests, Nationality India, and the results header reads 'Showing (1013) Hotels from Pattaya'. No error page, no empty form fields, no broken UI, no spinner — the search is unambiguously successful. The system status itself is recorded as SUCCESS, yet a CRITICAL rating was applied with no failure reason.
findings.ruleBookEntry: IF search status=SUCCESS AND results count > 0 AND no error page visible AND rating=CRITICAL with no failure reason → FALSE_POSITIVE_CRITICAL_RATING (eqis-side rating logic bug).
findings.eqisFixSuggestion: Audit the SearchPulse rating/scoring logic that converts a SUCCESS status into a CRITICAL rating; ensure that a successful result page with a non-zero hotel count cannot be downgraded to CRITICAL without an explicit, recorded failure reason. Add a guard: if httpStatus==SUCCESS and resultCount > 0 and failureReason is null, rating must not exceed WARNING.

findings.label: L2B Domestic | DEL→IXB | 4,562 searches
findings.rootCause: The search completed successfully with 74 results for DEL→IXB on 15 Jul 2026, but the run was rated CRITICAL despite no actual failure — the automation's result-validation or rating logic incorrectly flagged a successful search as a failure.
findings.evidence: All four frames (result screenshot + 3 video frames) show an identical, fully-loaded Etrav results page: 'Showing (74) Flights from New Delhi (DEL) to Bagdogra (IXB)', correct date 15 Jul'26, correct pax 1 Traveller Economy, cheapest fare ₹4,420.76 — no error page, no empty form fields, no blocked UI, no spinner. The recorded status is SUCCESS yet the rating is CRITICAL with no failure reason recorded, indicating the fault is in our post-search evaluation/rating code, not in Etrav.
findings.ruleBookEntry: IF search status=SUCCESS AND results page shows ≥1 flight AND no error page present BUT rating=CRITICAL with no failure reason → EQIS_FALSE_CRITICAL_RATING (eqis-side); check result-validator scoring logic.
findings.eqisFixSuggestion: Audit the post-search rating/scoring function that assigns CRITICAL to completed searches: ensure it only marks CRITICAL when status is genuinely non-SUCCESS or when a platform error is detected; add a guard that prevents CRITICAL rating when HTTP 200 results page with flight count > 0 is confirmed.

findings.label: L2B Domestic | BOM→CCU | 10,854 searches
findings.rootCause: The search completed successfully and 1086 results are visible on screen, but our result-detection logic failed to recognise them, incorrectly classifying the search as a failure due to a false positive on the loading-bar timeout check.
findings.evidence: All four frames (result screenshot + 3 final video frames) show a fully loaded Etrav results page: 'Showing (1086) Flights from Mumbai (BOM) to Kolkata (CCU)', cheapest fare ₹14,485 highlighted, multiple flight cards rendered with full details, no loading spinner or progress bar visible anywhere. The form fields (BOM→CCU, 24 Jun '26 / 14 Jul '26, 10 Travellers Economy) are correctly populated. There is no Etrav error page, no blank page, and no residual progress bar — the platform delivered results correctly.
findings.ruleBookEntry: IF results page shows 'Showing (N) Flights' AND flight cards are rendered AND no progress bar is visible, treat as SUCCESS regardless of prior loading-bar timeout flag — do NOT mark as FAILURE. (EQIS_FALSE_POSITIVE_RESULT_DETECTION)
findings.eqisFixSuggestion: In the result-detection logic, add a DOM check for the presence of the 'Showing (N) Flights' heading text or at least one flight-card element (e.g. CSS selector '.flight-card' or the result count label) BEFORE concluding a loading-bar timeout is a true failure. If the result count element is found and count > 0, override the timeout flag and mark the search as SUCCESS. Additionally, ensure the progress-bar disappearance check uses a MutationObserver or polling loop that re-checks after the bar's CSS transition ends, not just a fixed 60-second hard cutoff.

findings.label: L2B International | Harare | Hotel Search
findings.rootCause: The automation filled the destination ('Harare') and check-in date ('6 Sep'26') but never populated the Check-Out date field, leaving it as '–', which caused the form to block submission with 'Check-out date is required'.
findings.evidence: All four frames (3 video frames + 1 result screenshot) are identical: destination = 'Harare', Check-In = '6 Sep'26', Check-Out = '–' with a red 'Check-out date is required' validation error, Rooms & Guests = '1 Room / 2 Guests', Nationality = 'India'. The Search Hotel button was never successfully triggered because the checkout date step was skipped or the calendar interaction failed silently. The page never navigated away from the hotel search homepage.
findings.ruleBookEntry: IF hotel search form shows 'Check-out date is required' validation error AND Check-Out field contains '–' AND page remains on /hotels → EQIS_CHECKOUT_DATE_NOT_SET (eqis-side): automation failed to interact with or confirm the checkout date picker.
findings.eqisFixSuggestion: After setting the check-in date, explicitly open the checkout date calendar picker, click the correct checkout date cell, wait for the field to display a non-'–' value (assert field text !== '–' and !== ''), then proceed to click Search Hotel. Add a post-fill validation guard: if Check-Out field value is empty/dash, retry the date-picker interaction up to 2 times before marking the search as a pre-search failure.

findings.label: L2B Domestic | CCU→DEL | 3,593 searches
findings.rootCause: The search actually succeeded and returned 63 results on Etrav, but our result-detection logic failed to recognize the loaded results page within the 60-second timeout and incorrectly flagged it as a loading/timeout failure.
findings.evidence: All four frames (the result screenshot and all 3 final video frames) show a fully loaded Etrav results page displaying '63 Flights from Kolkata (CCU) to New Delhi (DEL)' with correct parameters (5 Travellers, Business Class, 21 Aug '26), multiple flight cards with prices, and no loading spinner or progress bar visible anywhere. The page is completely rendered and stable across all frames.
findings.ruleBookEntry: IF final frames show a fully rendered results page with flight cards AND result count header present AND no loading bar visible → mark as EQIS_RESULT_DETECTION_FALSE_NEGATIVE (eqis-side); the scraper/detector timed out before recognising the loaded state.
findings.eqisFixSuggestion: Improve the result-detection logic to check for the presence of the results count string (e.g., 'Showing (\d+) Flights') or individual flight card elements as a positive completion signal, rather than relying solely on the absence of a loading progress bar. Also consider raising the DOM-poll interval or adding a MutationObserver-based approach so results are detected as soon as they render, well within the 60-second window.
